per_question.question: How does the EPSDT special provision affect coverage for outpatient therapy services, and what ordering practitioner requirements apply to beneficiaries under 21?

One retrieved section came back empty/partial, so I’m getting the surrounding context and the child sections under the under-21 requirements to make sure I don’t miss any conditions.**Short answer:** For beneficiaries **under 21**, the **EPSDT special provision** can allow NC Medicaid to cover outpatient therapy services **even when the service exceeds a policy limitation**, so long as the service is within the federal EPSDT benefit and is **not** one of the excluded categories listed in the policy. The ordering practitioner must be one of the specific practitioner types listed in Policy 10A. No amendment was returned for the current version of this policy, so I’m citing the base policy as current and authoritative.

## 1) How EPSDT affects outpatient therapy coverage

Clinical Coverage Policy 10A includes a section titled **“EPSDT Special Provision: Exception to Policy Limitations for a Medicaid Beneficiary under 21 Years of Age.”** That section cites **42 U.S.C. § 1396d(r) [1905(r) of the Social Security Act]** and states that EPSDT does **not** require coverage for services:

- **“that is unsafe, ineffective, or experimental or investigational”**; or
- **“that is not medical in nature or not generally recognized as an accepted method of medical practice or treatment.”**

So, in practical terms, the **EPSDT special provision acts as an exception to policy limitations** for a Medicaid beneficiary under 21, but it does **not** override those two exclusions.  
**Source:** Clinical Coverage Policy 10A, Section 2.2.1 — “EPSDT Special Provision: Exception to Policy Limitations for a Medicaid Beneficiary under 21 Years of Age” (effective Feb. 1, 2025) [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

## 2) What this means for outpatient therapy services specifically

Policy 10A is the correct service-specific policy here because it is **“Outpatient Specialized Therapies.”** It includes a separate section for **beneficiaries under age 21** and a section on **medical necessity visit guidelines for beneficiaries under 21 years of age**. The policy text I retrieved shows that, for at least some therapy categories, NC Medicaid uses **medical-necessity-based ranges** rather than the adult-style fixed limitation structure.

For example, for **speech-language and audiology therapy**, the policy states:

- **Mild impairment:** **6 to 26** visits
- **Moderate impairment:** **up to 46** visits
- **Severe impairment:** **up to 52** visits
- The services are limited to the number of **medically necessary visits within an authorization period**
- An authorization period **cannot exceed six calendar months**
- For audiology: **30- to 60-minute sessions, one to three times a week, in increments of six calendar months**, with length and duration determined by severity and rate of change

**Source:** Clinical Coverage Policy 10A, Section 5.4.2 — “Speech-Language-Audiology Therapy” (effective Feb. 1, 2025) [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

Because the EPSDT section is expressly framed as an **exception to policy limitations** for beneficiaries under 21, it can matter when a child needs therapy beyond an ordinary policy limit. But based on the text I retrieved, I can only say definitively that the policy preserves coverage for under-21 beneficiaries subject to the exclusions above. I **did not retrieve fuller text spelling out the exact operational standard** for exceeding the visit ranges in Section 5.4, so I cannot add more detail beyond what the policy text returned.

## 3) Ordering practitioner requirements for beneficiaries under 21

Policy 10A has a specific section titled **“Ordering Practitioners.”** It lists the practitioners who may order outpatient specialized therapies:

- **Medical Doctor (MD)**
- **Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO)**
- **Doctor of Podiatric Medicine (DPM)**
- **Certified Nurse Midwife (CNM)**
- **Physician Assistant (PA)**
- **Nurse Practitioner (NP)**

The section I retrieved does **not** state a different ordering-practitioner list for beneficiaries under 21, so the policy text supports the conclusion that these are the ordering practitioners that apply, including for under-21 beneficiaries receiving outpatient therapy under Policy 10A.

**Source:** Clinical Coverage Policy 10A, Section 3.1.2 — “Ordering Practitioners” (effective Feb. 1, 2025) [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

## 4) Bottom line

- **EPSDT can expand coverage for outpatient therapy services for beneficiaries under 21 by creating an exception to policy limitations.**
- But EPSDT does **not** require coverage for services that are:
  - **unsafe, ineffective, experimental, or investigational**, or
  - **not medical in nature or not generally recognized as accepted medical practice**.
- For outpatient therapy under Policy 10A, orders must come from one of the listed practitioner types: **MD, DO, DPM, CNM, PA, or NP**.
- The current version I found is **Clinical Coverage Policy 10A, effective Feb. 1, 2025**, and **no amendments were returned** for that document.
